semantic_expectations.title: Literal cosine grid and source domain
semantic_expectations.expectation: Use integer d >= 2, real kappa >= 2, i = 1,...,d, theta_i = ((i-1/2) pi)/d, lambda_i(kappa) = (kappa+1)/2 + ((kappa-1)/2) cos(theta_i), and Lambda_kappa = diag(lambda_1(kappa),...,lambda_d(kappa)). The kappa=2 comparison is the specialization of this same grid, not an arbitrary symmetric matrix or another hard family.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: A generic matrix affine identity whose inputs are not tied to the literal cosine-grid precision matrices cannot alone discharge the selected source precursor.

semantic_expectations.title: Same rotation and actual precision identity
semantic_expectations.expectation: For one fixed orthogonal O, form A_kappa = O Lambda_kappa O^T and A_2 = O Lambda_2 O^T. Derive lambda_i(kappa) = (kappa-1) lambda_i(2) - (kappa-2), then Lambda_kappa = (kappa-1)Lambda_2 - (kappa-2)I_d, then the actual identity A_kappa = (kappa-1)A_2 - (kappa-2)I_d, using O I_d O^T = I_d. The rotation in both matrices must literally be the same O.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: An assumed affine sourcebridge, two unrelated rotations, an arbitrary hidden matrix, or a determinant-block construction cannot replace this derivation.

semantic_expectations.title: Forward actual matvec reply
semantic_expectations.expectation: For every x in R^d, if y_2 = A_2 x then y_kappa = (kappa-1)y_2 - (kappa-2)x equals A_kappa x. This is a reply for the source precision matrix at the same query point, using one exact matvec reply and known scalar arithmetic.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: A scalar polynomial identity, unsupported named reply, or existential relation with no A_kappa x equality is insufficient.

semantic_expectations.title: Reverse actual matvec reply with internal denominator discharge
semantic_expectations.expectation: Derive kappa-1 >= 1 > 0 from kappa >= 2, hence kappa-1 != 0 internally. For y_kappa = A_kappa x, the expression (kappa-1)^(-1) (y_kappa + (kappa-2)x) equals A_2 x for every x. The denominator condition is a derived proof ingredient, not a new source premise.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: Assuming kappa-1 != 0, assuming a reverse reply bridge, or suppressing the reciprocal factor changes the source contract.

semantic_expectations.title: Exact-real oracle meaning and pointwise scope
semantic_expectations.expectation: The precision input A specifies f_A(x) = (1/2)x^T A x and pi_A = N(0,A^(-1)); FO_A(x) = ((1/2)x^T A x, A x). A matvec reply gives the gradient and value (1/2)<x,Ax>, and a first-order reply contains Ax. The affine comparison concerns exact replies, not finite-precision arithmetic or an approximate oracle.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: A reply transport alone does not identify Gaussian laws, inverse precision matrices, total variation error, or a sampling output law.

semantic_expectations.title: Hidden eigenbasis versus target, randomness, and cost
semantic_expectations.expectation: The source samples O from Haar on O(d), independently of the algorithm seed; its spectrum is deterministic, may be known, and only the eigenbasis is hidden. Algorithms choose queries, stopping, and output as Borel functions of independent internal randomness and prior replies. Accuracy is uniform over inputs after averaging over the seed. Query budgets are deterministic caps for every input and every seed, not expected-query bounds. These are separate obligations from the pointwise matrix identity.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: Do not promote the source precursor into an adaptive-transcript simulation, Gaussian-target transport, TV transfer, finite-precision guarantee, or expected-cost identity without separate source-backed proofs.

semantic_expectations.title: Preserve main fixed theorem ranges and subsequent proof boundary
semantic_expectations.expectation: Theorem 4.1 has fixed delta in (0,1), threshold d_0(delta), every integer d >= d_0(delta), 2 <= kappa <= d^(1-delta), 0 < epsilon <= 1/10, and Q_G(d,kappa,epsilon) >= (delta/256) sqrt(kappa) log d. It holds when the spectrum is known and is not accuracy-growing as epsilon tends to zero. Remark 4.2 then refers separately to q-query output estimates from Lemma 4.4 and target moments from Lemma 4.5 with n=2q+1; the affine reply precursor alone does not prove this lower bound or these estimates.
semantic_expectations.audit_failure: Do not broaden to unbounded kappa, remove the d_0(delta) qualification, change epsilon range, or import the determinant-sign family/lower bound into the cosine-grid precursor.
